disproof_attempts: Origin/Host control: with a password configured, the origin-less branch returns true (auth.ts:196-199). The Host header is attacker-supplied and only has to match the bound authority, so this does not stop a network peer.

Exposure re-assessment on token change: reassessExposureFloor runs on every apply (auth-state onApplied), but assessHqExposure only considers browser tokens and password. Client tokens are not an input, so the floor stays false.

Periodic sweep closing tokenless clients: none found. sessionCleanupTimer (hq-server.ts:275-296) only prunes browser session entries. The watcher close loop is gated on hqClientAuthRequired, which is the flawed predicate itself.
requireAuthFloor latched whenever a password exists: no. It is latched only for exposure 'refuse' (hq-server.ts:157), which requires no password and no browser tokens.
ipAllowlist: optional and off by default (createHqIpAllowlist(options.ipAllowlist)); not a default control.

Accepted risk: SECURITY.md:212-216 defines OPEN MODE as empty token arrays AND no password, and SECURITY.md:265-268 repeats it. A password-protected, non-loopback HQ is by definition not open mode, and docs/subcommands/hq.md:891 says client token auth is enforced on /ws/client. Not an accepted risk.

Impact: an unauthenticated network peer can register sessions shown on the operator dashboard with spoofed telemetry, including approval prompts, which the operator may act on. It can also receive operator approve, answer-input and steer commands addressed to it, and take leader role for a project. Arbitrary execution is blocked by the control.execute token check (command-handlers.ts:167).
verdicts.owner_check: Regression test beside packages/cli/tests/hq-auth-floor.test.ts: auth.json with passwordHash plus one expired client token, non-loopback host; tokenless ws /ws/client upgrade must get 401. Fix: hqClientAuthRequired should also return true when hqAuthRequired(mutableAuth) is true, or when any client token ever existed.

Discoverability: client-token holders cannot use browser APIs (separate token sets). The only clientId sent to client sockets found is the lost leader's id in peer.* frames. A live victim's 8-hex-suffixed id is not exposed to /ws/client peers in the paths reviewed.

Design authority: SECURITY.md:234-236 says a stolen token grants its declared capabilities, and HQ targets a single operator's fleet ('Multi-tenant hostile environments are not the target'). If all client tokens belong to the same operator, a token holder already is the publisher principal.
Race: the victim publisher auto-reconnects, and its hello supersedes the attacker back, so impact is intermittent.
verdicts.blocker: Decisive unavailable fact: whether HQ client tokens are intended to be issued to mutually less-trusted principals (teammates or machines), and whether a live victim clientId is obtainable by a client-token holder. Source shows no channel exposing it to /ws/client peers.
